propositions: The N=3000 import benchmark calls author() 6,000 times via append_event, each invoking git config user.name via subprocess, consuming 47.79s of cumulative time.

The batch_stage_and_commit path calls sweep_stale_staging once per CREATE (3,000 times) while preparing a chunk, causing 375,876 redundant staging-owner checks within a single batch, consuming 15.94s.

Import-scoped caching of author name (keyed by fallback, contextvar-scoped, copy-on-write, nestable, reset in finally) reduces git config reads to 1 per import while preserving live lookup for interactive writes.

At most one stale-staging sweep per bounded batch (triggered on first new-ticket CREATE in that batch) reduces sweeps from 3,000 to 12 (one per CREATE chunk) while preserving sweep semantics for direct/interactive callers and empty/existing-ticket-only batches.

The controlled A/B harness (identical 3,000 creates, 3,000 comments, 29 total commits) with only these two mechanisms replaced as logical collaborators reduced wall time from 77.231s to 16.404s (60.8s delta, 78.8% improvement), discriminating these mechanisms from event serialization and commit-count alternatives.

The held-out RED oracle verified baseline calls (6000 author, 3000 sweeps) before fix and (1 author, 12 sweeps) after fix; independent defect mutations returned RED (no author scope, per-item sweep), confirming fix correctness without timing assertions.
